No Impact On Day To Day Operations'.

What changed: a structured restructuring of one subsidiary, with Bloomin' as the expected buyer for $26.3M (about 3% of the $0.9B market cap). Pre-market on the consolidated tape: 10.62, +0.4% on 20,712 shares.

memos.headline: BLMN: no trade. A subsidiary's pre-arranged Chapter 11
Marvell will buy Lumentum in a $115B all-stock deal, 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share
reasoning: Source: the companies' joint announcement (Dow Jones via Morningstar; Benzinga 08:02 ET): 'Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 shares of Marvell common stock for each share of Lumentum stock ... a premium of approximately 23.9% ... unanimously approved by the boards'. Lumentum holders get about 33% of the combined company. Lumentum was halted at 06:57 ET and quoted again from 07:25.
What changed: Lumentum stops being an independent optical-component company. Its value is now tied to Marvell's share price.

Pre-market on the consolidated tape: LITE 783.52, -6.8% from 840.81, on 778,275 shares; MRVL 189.01, -3.8% from 196.40, on 2.87M shares. At 4.5 x 189.01 the deal is worth 850.55 a Lumentum share, so LITE trades 7.9% below it. Both fell sharply on Friday (LITE -8.6%, MRVL -10%) before the announcement.
objections: Friday's falls in both names before the announcement are unexplained.

memos.headline: No single-name edge: LITE now trades as Marvell stock plus a 7.9% deal-risk spread
reasoning: What changed: LITE's value is 4.5 x MRVL if the deal closes. The 7.9% gap to that value is large for an agreed deal, and it prices real risk: a $115B semiconductor combination needs antitrust review in several countries, China's included, and a long closing period.

A long LITE is a long MRVL position plus a bet the spread narrows. Without shorting MRVL against it, which the crew's single-leg brackets cannot do, most of the risk is Marvell's own price, which fell 10% Friday and 3.8% this morning.
A short on LITE or MRVL bets on deal failure or more selling of the buyer. There is no information yet on regulatory pushback, and the buyer has already marked down 14% over two sessions.
Would prove this wrong: the spread collapsing to under 3% within days (the market dismissing regulatory risk) or widening past 15% (pricing a likely break). Either would be a new event to judge.
objections: Merger arbitrage; the crew cannot hold a hedged pair.

memos.headline: LITE: no trade. Merger arbitrage at a 7.9% spread
reasoning: Check later: the LITE/MRVL spread (LITE vs 4.5 x MRVL) on 11/09. A big agreed deal priced at about 8% below terms is a datapoint on how the market prices large-cap antitrust risk.
Same call as RRC/EQT last week.
